import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'serif',
    'font.serif': ['Times New Roman', 'Times', 'DejaVu Serif'],
    'mathtext.fontset': 'dejavuserif',
})

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(3.4, 2.4))

p = np.linspace(0.001, 0.5, 1000)

curves = [
    (4,  '#1f77b4', '-',  1.2, 'K=4'),
    (8,  '#d62728', '-',  2.0, 'K=8'),
    (16, '#2ca02c', '-',  1.2, 'K=16'),
]

for K, color, ls, lw, label in curves:
    P_correct = p / (1 - (1 - p)**K)
    ax.plot(p * 100, P_correct * 100, color=color, linestyle=ls,
            linewidth=lw, label=label, zorder=3)

# Large-K limit diagonal: P_correct = p
ax.plot(p * 100, p * 100, color='#888888', linestyle='--', linewidth=1.0,
        label='$K{\\to}\\infty$ limit', zorder=2)

# Random chance line
ax.axhline(y=50, color='#AAAAAA', linestyle=':', linewidth=0.8, zorder=1)
ax.text(48, 52, 'random chance', fontsize=8, color='#999999', ha='right', va='bottom')

# Shaded region: typical agent task range (p < 20%)
ax.axvspan(0, 20, alpha=0.08, color='#4477AA', zorder=0)
ax.text(10, 95, 'typical agent\ntask range', fontsize=8, color='#6699BB',
        ha='center', va='top', style='italic')

# ALFWorld vertical line at p=12.5%
ax.axvline(x=12.5, color='#888888', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.7, alpha=0.6, zorder=1)

# Mark the K=8, p=12.5% intersection
p_alf = 0.125
K8 = 8
P_correct_alf = p_alf / (1 - (1 - p_alf)**K8) * 100
ax.plot(12.5, P_correct_alf, 'o', color='#d62728', markersize=5, zorder=5,
        markeredgecolor='white', markeredgewidth=0.8)
ax.annotate(f'19.1%\n(ALFWorld,\n$p$=12.5%)',
            xy=(12.5, P_correct_alf),
            xytext=(25, 25),
            fontsize=8, ha='left', va='center', color='#d62728',
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#d62728', lw=1.0,
                          connectionstyle='arc3,rad=0.2'))

ax.set_xlabel('Episode success rate $p$ (%)', fontsize=11)
ax.set_ylabel('$P(\\mathrm{correct\\ sign} \\mid \\mathrm{update})$ (%)', fontsize=11)
ax.set_xlim(0, 50)
ax.set_ylim(0, 100)
ax.tick_params(labelsize=9)

ax.grid(True, alpha=0.2, linewidth=0.5, color='#CCCCCC')

ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

plt.tight_layout(pad=0.3)
plt.savefig('fig_theory_curve.pdf', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=300)
plt.savefig('fig_theory_curve.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=200)
print('Saved fig_theory_curve.pdf and .png')

The paper discusses Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), exemplified by Search-R1, which offers fast convergence and a value-free formulation but consistently suffers from training collapse. The authors identify Lazy Likelihood Displacement (LLD)—a systematic reduction or stagnation in the likelihood of both correct and incorrect responses—as the core mechanism driving this failure.
